title: Abdullah ibn Umar
hookLine: followed the Prophet's footsteps so closely he prayed where he had prayed

lines: A BEND, A TREE, A VALLEY.
cards: On the long road between Medina and Mecca there are spots with nothing special about them. A bend. A tree.
A patch of ground by a valley. Travelers pass them without a glance. One traveler kept stopping.

Nafi', who learned from him, tells it in Sahih al-Bukhari: Abdullah ibn Umar would halt at certain places and pray there, because he had seen the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, pray in those very places.
Today: the son of Umar, walking in someone else's footprints.

teach.b: Abdullah was the son of Umar ibn al-Khattab. What his students passed on was how closely he watched, and how closely he copied.
Bukhari gives a whole run of reports from Nafi' naming the places on the pilgrimage road where Ibn Umar prayed, each one a spot where the Prophet had prayed before him.
Another scene in Bukhari shows what kind of follower he was. As a young man, Abdullah slept in the mosque. He dreamed that two angels took him to the Fire, and he was afraid.

teach.h: IF ONLY HE PRAYED AT NIGHT.
teach.b: He told his sister Hafsah, and she told the Prophet, who said: what an excellent man Abdullah is, if only he would pray at night. His son Salim adds one line: after that, Abdullah slept only a little of the night.
One sentence of praise, one gentle if only, and the shape of his nights changed. Later scholars asked what kind of following this was.

teach.h: WORSHIP, OR JUST WHERE HE STOPPED?
teach.b: Some distinguish between what the Prophet did as worship and teaching, and what he did simply as a traveler, such as where he happened to stop. Some readers see Ibn Umar following both kinds, out of love.
Either way, the picture stays: a man who wanted his feet to land where the footsteps were.

how: Muslims follow the sunnah, the Prophet's example, in worship and in small daily habits; scholars distinguish acts done as worship from those done by custom, and people differ on how far to follow the second kind.

o: Umar himself, the caliph, known by a short name
a grandson of Umar who gathered the hadith
the son of Umar, who prayed where the Prophet prayed

games.q: Abdullah ibn Umar — tap the pairs.
p: named the places where he prayed
told the Prophet about his dream
said he slept little after that

s: Ibn Umar prayed on the road where the Prophet had prayed
Nafi' names those places in Bukhari.
the Prophet ordered everyone to pray at those same spots
Nafi's reports say he prayed there because he had seen the Prophet pray there; they give no such command.
Ibn Umar was scolded into praying at night
he was praised: what an excellent man, if only he prayed at night. that was enough.

games.q: you're young Abdullah. word reaches you that the Prophet said: what an excellent man, if only he prayed at night. what do you do?
o: feel proud of the praise and carry on.
start praying at night, and sleep only a little.
ask your sister what he really meant.
games.why: his son Salim says that after that, Abdullah slept only a little of the night.

practice: Choose one small sunnah, a habit the Prophet is reported to have kept, that you'll actually do: some Muslims begin with smiling at people they meet, entering the mosque right foot first, as Ibn Umar himself is reported to have done, saying bismillah before they eat, or giving with the right hand.
Picture the moment it will happen, and see yourself doing it. If you pray, you can ask to follow well.

wordCard.voice: Ibn Umar, son of Umar ibn al-Khattab, who prayed where the Prophet had prayed and, after one if only, rose to pray at night. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the way, the example; for Muslims, the Prophet's example in word and deed.

carryVoice: Your line: in his footsteps. Small steps, copied out of love. That's day eight hundred thirty-nine.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 483–492 (Nafi': places on the road where Ibn Umar prayed because the Prophet had)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1121–1122 (the dream; 'what an excellent man Abdullah is, if only he prayed at night'; Salim: he slept little after)
